newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy's Prodi says interest rates must fall fast.
newsitem.headline: Italy's Prodi says interest rates must fall fast.

text.p: Prime Minister Romano Prodi, preparing a tough budget for 1997, said on Wednesday that everything was at stake for the Italian economy over the next few months and its only hope was lower interest rates fast.
"Either we have a radical, immediate fall in interest rates and the cost of money, or the route to salvation is blocked," he told a meeting of self-employed artisans.

Prodi said bank interest rates were too high and the system was inefficient and should be reformed. The Bank of Italy cut its discount rate by three-quarters of a point to 8.25 percent in July after keeping it unchanged for more than a year.

Prodi's centre-left Olive Tree coalition must present its 1997 budget to parliament before the end of the month. The government has already said it aims to cut 32.4 trillion ($21 billion) lire off Italy's deficit next year.

"This budget must be the one to take us back into Europe -- I would never forgive myself if we failed," said Prodi, who has vowed to take the lira back into Europe's Exchange Rate Mechanism as soon as possible and to be among the first countries to join a planned single currency in 1999.
"Everything's at stake in these months," he said, adding the government faced "a very tough road of transition".
The government is expected to unveil its budget package on September 27 and parliament must approve it by the year's end.

Fabio Mussi, leader of the ex-communist Democratic Party of the Left in the lower Chamber of Deputies told reporters ater a meeting with Prodi that the budget would be "serious and severe but as balanced as possible in the sharing out of sacrifices".
